text:
rahul_sales: FYI — AcmeCorp negotiating 12mo commit. They expect a steady baseline plus spikes: baseline ~300 RPS chat (avg 16 tokens/turn), spikes up to 1,200 RPS for 15-20m during business hours. Want proposal: reserved GPUs, autoscale policy, burst credits, price impact. Also asking about security controls for PII and SOC2.

rahul_sales: Need a quick capacity plan and a short checklist for security / presales Qs to attach to the quote.

(tina_se joined the thread)

tina_se: quick Qs — is that 300 RPS sustained per second or 300 requests per minute? also are embeddings called in the same path or separate?

rahul_sales: 300 RPS sustained, embeddings are a separate background job (approx 40 RPS) but some requests call both (chat -> embedding for rerank ~30% of requests).

kevin_eng_platform: rough estimate approach: we need concurrency → avg request length, tokens per response, and KV cache hit-rate. If avg response is 160 tokens and model latency target is <1500ms, baseline throughput numbers change. Can you confirm average response tokens?

rahul_sales: average response ~140 tokens, suggest planning for 200 tokens to be safe. Latency SLO is P50 < 400ms for chat simple flows, P95 < 1200ms.

kevin_eng_platform: ok. Back-of-envelope: plan capacity for 300 RPS baseline + 20% buffer = 360 RPS. For spikes, support up to 1,200 RPS for 20 minutes with autoscale + burst pool. Recommendation: reserved pool sized for baseline (360 RPS) and a burst pool of prewarmed instances that can scale to handle the spike for 30 minutes before autoscale completes.

kevin_eng_platform: Suggested concrete config (will validate with perf team):
```yaml
reserved_pool: 8 x A100
prewarm_burst: 4 x A100 (cold-warm prewarm to accept traffic in <30s)
autoscale_max: 12 x A100
kv_cache: enabled (prefix caching for top-10 intents)
batching: target tokens_per_batch=4096, adaptive=true
```

jess_ops: ops notes — AZ affinity: put reserved pool in 2 AZs for resiliency. Preheat window: run periodic preheat jobs 10m before expected spikes. Use spot fallback for additional capacity but gate it behind lower-priority SLA and always have N+1 reserved to meet SLA.

maya_cs: security checklist from customer: KMS key mgmt, audit logs retention 12 months, SOC2 report, data isolation for embeddings, and ability to delete PII on request. We can provide SOC2 and audit logs; need to confirm KMS integration (bring-your-own-key) for Private customers.

kevin_eng_platform: confirm: for Private we support BYOK via KMS/HSM; Hosted API can integrate with customer-managed keys for dedicated customers — ops will confirm exact region availability. Also we can add request-level encryption metadata in audit logs.

rahul_sales: pricing ask — if they commit $120k/month, what discount tiers and how many reserved GPUs should we propose? They care about effective per-token cost and want a burst cushion without paying full reserved for peak.

finance_bot: quick calc — propose hybrid commit: 70% of committed spend mapped to reserved baseline, 20% allocated to burst credits, 10% remaining for overage at metered rate. Example: $120k -> $84k baseline + $24k burst credits + $12k overage cap. Exact GPU count depends on mapping (see platform).

kevin_eng_platform: mapping example (need perf validation): 8 reserved A100 could cover baseline (360 RPS with KV caching + batching) with autoscale to 12 for spikes. Burst credits purchase would pay for the prewarm 4x A100 and short extra runtime during spikes. If they want <500ms P50 we should upsell +2 reserved GPUs.

tina_se: for the POC: propose a 72hr load test using our traffic generator with their production sample (sanitized). Will run three phases: baseline ramp, scheduled spike windows, chaos (AZ failover). Need a signed NDA to ingest sample.

jess_ops: runbook snippets to include in the POC deliverable:
- preheat cron: `0 */4 * * * /preheat --pool reserved --minutes 15`
- autoscale policy: `scale_up_threshold: 70% gpu_util` -> add one instance every 30s, cooldown 5m
- fallback: spot_enable: true, fallback_order: [spot, burst_pool]

maya_cs: customer also wants a short SLA clause around reserved uptime for the commit. We should provide a 99.9% reserved availability SLA with defined maintenance windows. Ops — can we commit to that?

jess_ops: 99.9% for reserved pool is OK, with scheduled maintenance windows and cross-AZ redundancy. Will have legal draft for SLA language.

rahul_sales: blockers: 1) need exact perf numbers per GPU validated by eng 2) security answers for KMS + embeddings retention 3) pricing mapping to reserved GPU counts.

kevin_eng_platform: I'll run perf bench next 24h with model variant they expect and confirm tokens/sec per A100 and KV cache impact. Expect numbers by EOD tomorrow.

maya_cs: I'll upload SOC2 and standard security artifacts to the shared drive and draft short answers for the security questionnaire.

finance_bot: I'll prepare two quote variants: conservative (8 reserved, 4 burst) and aggressive (10 reserved, 6 burst) with the hybrid credit mapping. Delivery by tomorrow noon.

rahul_sales: action items summarized: 1) kevin — perf validation (EOD tomorrow) 2) jess — draft SLA + ops runbook (tomorrow) 3) maya — security pack and short answers (today) 4) finance_bot — two quote variants (tomorrow noon)

rahul_sales: thanks all — I’ll sync with AcmeCorp on NDA and sample data. Ping here with updates. :thumbsup:
